definition: Asian options are approximated using a modified Black 76 formula with an adjusted volatility input, since the true distribution of an averaged price series is not exactly lognormal.
core_idea: The average of several lognormal price distributions is not itself lognormal, so exact closed-form pricing isn't possible, but a modified Black 76 approach with adjusted volatility gives a reasonably good approximation outside the delivery/averaging period.
key_points: Outside the delivery month, an adjusted-volatility version of Black 76 is used as an approximation.
Within the delivery month, part of the averaging period's prices are already known/observed, so the model must calculate the expected dispersion of the remaining unobserved prices.
As more of the averaging period's prices become known during the delivery month, expected volatility declines rapidly.
trading_implications: Risk on an Asian option should be expected to fall quickly as the delivery/averaging month progresses and more of the settlement prices are locked in.
caveats: The author notes the average of lognormal distributions is not itself lognormal — an exact analytic solution isn't available, only an approximation.
